text:
maria: Hey team — I sketched a tiny runbook for tenant isolation during dedicated onboarding. goal is a single-page flow engineers can reference during provisioning and incident triage. PTAL?

tim: Nice. Can you call out the exact failure modes we want to document? preemption, eviction, noisy-tenant throttling, and cross-tenant KV-cache leakage?

maria: Yep — included: preemption -> fallback model, eviction -> reserved-pool reclaim steps, noisy-tenant -> burst-limits & label changes, and cache leakage -> KV invalidation steps.

alex: Can you paste the state machine you mentioned? quick ascii is fine.

maria: Sure — added below:

"""
STATE: provisioning_requested
  -> validate_tenant_labels -> (ok) allocate_reserved_pool -> provisioning_in_progress
  provisioning_in_progress
  -> capacity_ok -> active
  -> capacity_constrained -> trigger_fallback_policy -> active (reduced capacity)
  -> eviction_detected -> mark_isolated -> migrate_to_reserved_pool -> active
  active
  -> noisy_signals -> apply_rate_limits -> monitor_30m -> (stable) or (escalate)
"""

sam: Love the state machine. Two quick asks: 1) add the CLI command we expect oncall to run for forced-migration; 2) include the SDK snippet for setting tenant labels.

maria: Added both. CLI: `rci tenant migrate --tenant-id T123 --target-pool reserved-pool-2 --reason "eviction"`

maria: SDK snippet (python):

```python
from redwood import DedicatedClient
client = DedicatedClient(api_key=os.environ["REDWOOD_KEY"])
client.tenants.update_labels("T123", {"isolation":"reserved-pool-2", "sla":"gold"})
```

tim: Quick wording nit: for the CLI step, document that migration is async and to check `rci tenant status T123` until `state=active`.

maria: done. also added a tiny YAML example for autoscale fallback policy we can copy into docs: 

```yaml
fallback_policy:
  name: regional-fallback
  triggers:
    - condition: capacity_utilization >= 0.92
      action: route_to_variant
      params:
        variant: quantized-128
        max_routing_pct: 30
  cooldown_sec: 300
```

alex: That YAML looks good. We should add an explicit note on latency SLO tradeoffs when routing to `quantized-128`. maybe a short table?

maria: I added a one-line callout: "Routing to quantized variants can save cost but increase 95p latency by 20–60ms depending on model family."

sam: Also, there's a stale link in the current handbook to the isolation design doc — it's pointing to internal google doc. Can you replace with the archived RFC link? I left the link: https://rwd.com/rfc/isolation-2025

maria: replaced. updated anchors and added permalink to the RFC.

docs-bot: new file draft uploaded: /handbook/dedicated/mini-runbook-isolation.md (draft). Preview: https://preview.redwood/docs/handbook/dedicated/mini-runbook-isolation

tim: Great. Can we add a short checkbox checklist for oncall steps (5 bullets) so folks don't miss the migrate -> invalidate-cache -> confirm -> close loop sequence?

maria: added checklist: 1) `rci tenant status` 2) `rci tenant migrate` 3) `rci cache invalidate` 4) monitor traces & latency 5) reopen if errors persist.

alex: One more thing — make the SDK snippet language-agnostic by adding a Go example. That helps platform teams.

maria: done:

```go
client := redwood.NewDedicatedClient(ctx, redis.Options{Addr: "..."})
_, err := client.Tenants.UpdateLabels(ctx, "T123", map[string]string{"isolation":"reserved-pool-2", "sla":"gold"})
```

sam: LGTM. I also pushed a minor SLA phrasing tweak: change "best-effort" to "best-effort within reserved pool constraints" — avoids legal confusion.

maria: thanks — applied.

alex: who wants to own the PR? small edits left: add a short note about metrics to watch (`tenant_cpu`, `kv_cache_miss_rate`, `inflight_requests`).

maria: I'll open the PR in ~30m and assign to @tim + @alex for review. PR name: "docs: mini runbook — tenant isolation and fallback snippets"

tim: I'll review after stand. If you want faster merge, add me as reviewer and tag @oncall if it's urgent.

docs-bot: PR created: https://github.com/redwood/inference-docs/pull/4128 (maria:docs/mini-runbook-isolation)

maria: thanks. last ask: can someone sanity-check the cooldown_sec value (300s) and the max_routing_pct (30%)?

sam: cooldown 300s is fine for regional fallbacks, maybe lower for global panic. I'll leave a comment in the PR with a variant (120s) for global.

alex: max_routing_pct 30% seems conservative — ok for gradual rollout. fine from docs side.

maria: perfect. I'll merge once reviews are in and then backport a short summary to the Dedicated onboarding checklist page.

sam: thanks — huge improvement. :shipit:
